html:
Zoroastrianism is the ancient Iranian religion founded on the teaching of the prophet Zoroaster, or Zarathustra. When he lived is disputed, with guesses from about 1500 to 600 BCE.

It teaches that one wise god, Ahura Mazda, made a good world, which is attacked by a destructive spirit, Angra Mainyu. Every person chooses a side through good thoughts, good words and good deeds. At the end of time evil will be defeated, the dead will rise and all will be judged. Fire, as a sign of purity, is kept burning in fire temples. The scripture is the Avesta, whose oldest hymns, the Gathas, are credited to Zoroaster himself. Its oldest texts come from the world of the Iranian-speaking herders of Central Asia.

It became the faith of Iran's great empires:

  • The Achaemenid kings called on Ahura Mazda in their inscriptions.
  • The Parthians honoured it while tolerating other faiths.
  • The Sasanians made it a state church, with a powerful priesthood.

After the Arab conquests of the 600s, Iran slowly became Muslim. Some Zoroastrians settled in Gujarat, where they became the Parsis. Perhaps 100,000 to 200,000 remain, mostly in India and Iran. Its ideas of heaven and hell, judgement and a coming saviour may have shaped Judaism, Christianity and Islam, though how much is debated. The god Mithra, from the same world, gave his name to Roman Mithraism.
sum: Zoroastrianism is the ancient Iranian religion founded on the teaching of the prophet Zoroaster, or Zarathustra. When he lived is disputed, with guesses from about 1500 to 600 BCE.
